title: H3b: wire decision routes into the daemon — routine holds and closable goals handled without a model launch, investigate on the configured smaller tier, escalate on the premium tier; one coalesced decision packet per goal per tick with a durable processed-event cursor and infra backoff
spec:
Build on goal/T-0353 after H3a (T-0357 decision.py), H2 (T-0361 launch attribution) and H7 (T-0364 failure kinds). Handover sections 3 and 4. Evidence (scout T-0354): daemon.py:1044-1049 launches one headless Planner per decision point whenever planner.autonomous is true; planner_runs.decision_points yields one point per held task; tick breaks after one launch per tick (rate throttle, no content coalescing); no processed-event cursor; _record_failed_launch treats auth, quota and unavailable failures like any failure (gave_up after 2).
1. planner_runs.run (or its caller in daemon.tick): build ctx for decision.route from bus state (complexity, task_class via scorecard.task_class, hold_reason, failure_signature and repeat flag, auto rounds used, spec review rounds, scout counts and blocked flags, gate state, review triggers from daemon._review_plan's lists, infra kind from pool cooldowns); route each point; routine -> no launch, the daemon's existing machinery acts (auto_fix_round; for closable: deterministic close = retrospective entry via the memory record script with facts from bus state and a no-new-learning marker when nothing new, PR opened from a fixed template with task titles, merged shas, gate result and scorecard numbers, GOAL task result posted with the PR url); investigate -> launch on [planner.routes].investigate_tier with the same packet; escalate -> launch on the premium tier. Route, reason, evidence and cheaper_steps go into the claim record (H2 fields). [planner.routes].enabled = false restores the previous per-point escalation.
2. Coalescing: all points of one goal in the same tick collapse into one decision packet (sections per point, ordered held first), one claim keyed goal id plus a state version = sha12 over the sorted (task id, status, hold_reason, merged_into, last event seq) of the goal's children; an identical version never launches again (the durable no-duplicate guarantee); the cursor (last processed bus event seq per goal) is persisted in planner_runs.json and the packet lists events since the cursor. Unrelated goals never share a packet; a blocked scout or a security hold is not delayed by coalescing (it launches in the same tick).
3. Infra backoff: launch failures whose stderr or exit signature matches auth, quota or service-unavailable markers set a cooldown on the account (pool.cooldown with reason) and are not counted toward gave_up; the point is retried after the cooldown without a model call in between; notify once per transition (H4's map).
4. Soft premium budget: when a goal's escalate launches exceed [planner.routes].premium_launches_soft_per_goal, the launch still happens and the claim record carries exception: true with the reason; never fake completion or skip a needed launch.
Tests in tests/test_planner_runs.py and tests/test_daemon.py: test_routine_hold_launches_no_model, test_closable_all_merged_closes_without_launch (PR template filled, GOAL result posted), test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier, test_escalate_uses_premium_tier_with_reason, test_same_state_version_never_relaunches, test_burst_of_holds_one_packet_per_goal, test_two_goals_two_packets, test_auth_failure_cools_account_without_gave_up, test_soft_budget_exceeded_still_launches_with_exception, test_routes_disabled_restores_per_point_launch. Keep every existing test green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; git add -A and commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs.py and tests/test_daemon.py: test_routine_hold_launches_no_model, test_closable_all_merged_closes_without_launch, test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier, test_escalate_uses_premium_tier_with_reason, test_same_state_version_never_relaunches, test_burst_of_holds_one_packet_per_goal, test_two_goals_two_packets, test_auth_failure_cools_account_without_gave_up, test_soft_budget_exceeded_still_launches_with_exception, test_routes_disabled_restores_per_point_launch pass
many idle ticks with unchanged state produce zero launches (covered by test_same_state_version_never_relaunches plus the existing idle test)
every launch record carries route, reason, evidence, cheaper_steps, state version and cursor
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

spec_review_risks.issue: ctx-building instructions (item 1) never populate failing_ids, in_scope_review_comments, auto_fix_rounds (cap), touches_auth/migrations/interfaces/data_deletion, or scouts_done's security_trigger/semantic_trigger — all required by decision.route() (orchestrator/decision.py:88-118,120-137), whose unknown() helper fails closed to 'escalate' when any is missing. None of these fields exist anywhere in the codebase outside decision.py and its test. As specified, routine/investigate routes for held and scouts_done points are unreachable, so test_routine_hold_launches_no_model and test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier cannot pass.

routine routes explicitly skip the goal_id+state_version claim mechanism (item 2 scopes that dedup to launches only), but the closable routine path performs external side effects (open a PR via gh, post the GOAL task result). No goal-closed stamp exists anywhere in goals.py, and daemon.py's own stage-stamp convention (module docstring: 'a stage runs at most once no matter how often tick() runs') is not invoked here. Without an equivalent guard, every tick while the goal stays closable re-opens a duplicate PR and re-posts the GOAL result.

the new goal_id+state_version claim scheme isn't reconciled with the existing (goal_id, kind, payload_key) dedup keys and per-kind blocking rules documented at the top of the file and implemented in _find_record/_blocked. The spec doesn't say whether old per-point records and the new per-goal coalesced record coexist, share a kind, or replace the old scheme, risking two launches locking at different granularities on the same goal.

no stated timing for when the per-goal event cursor advances relative to launch success. If it advances before a launch is confirmed, an infra-backoff retry (item 3, meant to replay 'without a model call in between') would rebuild its packet from 'events since cursor' with fewer events than the original attempt saw.
